title: Urinary proteomics to guide early intervention to prevent complications in type 2 diabetes – a feasibility study
official: SIGNAL - Body fluid proteome SIGnatures for persoNALised intervention to prevent cardiovascular and renal complications in diabetes
summary: Main objective: To explore the feasibility of using urinary proteomic signatures in clinical practice to identify patients at risk of developing end organ damage and identify which patients should receive additional reno-cardiovascular protective treatment. We will use urinary proteomic classifiers: CKD273, CAD160 and HF2 to identify patients suited for additional medical treatment with sodium-glucose-cotransporter-2-inhibitors, glucagon-like-peptide-1 receptor agonists or non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men and women over 18 years of age.
2. Type 2 diabetes with no clinical signs of HF NYHA Class IV
3. Able to understand the written participant information and give informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Heart failure NYHA class IV at screening
2. Serum potassium > 5.0 mmol/L at the screening visit if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is finerenone
3. Addison’s Disease, if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is finerenone
4. Concomitant treatment with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, nelfinavir, cobicistat, clarithromycin, telithromycin, nefazodone) if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is finerenone
5. Treatment with a potassium-sparing diuretic (amiloride, triamterene) if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is finerenone
6. Treatment with other mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist than finerenone (e.g., spironolactone, eplerenone, esaxerenone, canrenone), if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is finerenone
7. Elevated Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) > 3x upper normal limit, autoimmune hepatitis, and/or severe hepatic impairment (including but not limited to a history of hepatic encephalopathy, a history of oesophageal varices or a history of portocaval shunt.)
8. Autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease
9. Lupus nephritis or ANCA-associated vasculitis, or any other primary or secondary kidney disease requiring immunosuppressive therapy within 6 months prior to screening
10. Kidney transplant or dialysis
11. Severe or proliferative retinopathy or retinal bleeding, macular edema within 6 months prior to the screening visit, if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is semaglutide.
12. eGFR < 25 ml/min/1.73m2 at the screening visit
13. Any other history, condition, therapy, or uncontrolled intercurrent illness that could, as judged by the investigator, affect participant safety or compliance with study requirements.
14. Known or suspected severe abuse of narcotics
15. Participant in another intervention study with medicinal product
16. Vulnerable (i.e., under guardianship) or mentally incapacitated subjects (i.e., not able to understand and sign the informed consent
17. A female who is pregnant, breastfeeding, or intends to become pregnant, or women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) who are not using highly effective contraceptive methods.
18. Receiving therapy with all three of the study medication prior to enrolment.
19. Myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 12 weeks prior to enrolment
20. Known or suspected hypersensitivity to all three of the study medications or related products
21. History of acute pancreatitis within 6 months prior to the screening visit
22. Body mass index < 18.5 kg/m2 at the screening visit if the only possible therapy addition at the screening visit is semaglutide
23. Type 1 diabetes
